chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, raising it, from one of the two (peace be upon them) who said:
You should say, whenever you plant or sow,
The parable of a good word is like a good tree, whose root is firm and whose branches are in the sky. It yields its fruit at every time by the permission of its Lord.

key_terms.بِإِذْنِ رَبِّها: By the permission of its Lord

ai.seo_question: What should be recited when planting trees or crops in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this practice as a recommended act (mustahabb) linking agricultural labor with spiritual mindfulness, reflecting the Shia emphasis on integrating daily activities with dhikr. The metaphor of the 'good tree' (Shajarah Tayyibah) is traditionally interpreted by scholars like Al-Allama al-Tabarsi as representing the declaration of faith (Kalimat al-Tawhid) or the Imams themselves, whose teachings provide continuous spiritual sustance. This narration underscores the concept that righteous actions, like planting, yield enduring fruits through divine permission (bi-idhn Rabbiha).
